articles.content: Baker Hughes US oil rig count rises 1 to 460. Total rigs unchanged at 603 US expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian products as soon as today - report UMich final October final consumer sentiment 48.0 vs 46.3 expected Canada August retail sales +1.2% vs +1.3% expected US S&P Global flash October services PMI 57.9 vs 58.0 expected Markets: Gold down $24 to $3999 WTI crude oil up $4.01 to $103.47 S&P 500 down 0.5% US 10-year yields up 4.6 bps to 5.00% AUD leads, CHF lags There are heavy cross-currents working their way through markets at the moment. The latest one is the oil market spiking into the weekend, including brent hitting the highest since May at $117. There are growing signs that Trump will escalate versus Iran in an attempt to break the deadlock and shuffle the deck on terrible polls ahead of the midterms. In a rally just before the close he said they may do a "little Epic Fury" and that fits with some reports about a short-term bombing campaign on nuclear sites and some infrastructure. Markets will be closely watching what happens afte the close and then the focus will turn to potential retaliation from Iran. The jump in oil prices lifted Treasury yields and weighed on gold but it wasn't the only focus. The euro continues to be dragged down by protests in France and elsewhere. The market is sniffing out political change and the likelihood of more government spending in order to tamp down on unrest and preserve the status quo. Meanwhile, the AI trade remains in flux with the market increasingly focused on where all the money will come from to finance it all. The answer appears to be via equity markets and no one is sure if they can sustain that kind of capital raising. Already, we've seen the bond market shudder so I'm skeptical. Meta fell another 1% after yesterday's 7% decline as it readies itself to launch a new class of shares. Other losers were telco names on signs that Elon Musk will is moving Starlink to earth where he will install cell phone towers, or buy space on existing ones. Have a great weekend. This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

See everything new and updated in Honda’s 2027 SUV and truck lineup here. Japanese automaker made huge investments As it recalculates its future approach, Honda keeps its 2027 SUV and truck lineup mostly the same as it was last year, with one exception: more off-road-oriented equipment for the popular Passport. See those changes and everything else new for 2027 here. Although a refreshed or next-generation CR-V is anticipated to arrive soon, the compact SUV gets no major changes for 2027. Last year, theand wireless charging pad as standard equipment. The EX-L trim received a larger gauge cluster display. Get ready, badge sales for Comic-Con 2027 happen in three weeks The optional AWD system was retuned for better traction. Look for a big update to the CR-V Hybrid in the next year or two. For 2027, though, it’s just like it was in 2026, when it received changes including a larger touchscreen, wireless charging pad, improved AWD system, and a bigger digital gauge display on certain trims. The off-road-inspired. It gains new suspension springs and dampers, control arms, stabilizer bars, knuckles, front driveshafts, and a front subframe. These add 1.4 inches of ground clearance for a total of 9.65 inches, while also improving approach, departure, and breakover angles. Outside, the 2027 Passport TrailSport looks more rugged thanks to amber LED lights integrated into the hood scoop. The lower front bumper is revised, and the fender flares become broader. With the available Blackout package, more black exterior trim is applied. All TrailSport models now have the TrailWatch 360-degree camera system and a heated steering wheel; these were previously exclusive to the TrailSport Elite trim. Additionally, the Honda Trail Experience app adds real-time vehicle information, video recording, and trail data overlays. , the Pilot three-row SUV is unlikely to see major changes for 2027. The TrailSport model also gains access to the Honda Trail Experience app. Honda has confirmed it’sfor 2028 or 2029. It’s anticipated to get tougher styling, more rugged capability, new functionality features, and improved tech. A hybrid powertrainAs it worked to develop its own EVs, Honda licensed General Motors’ electric vehicle platform to create the Prologue. The SUV was just a Chevrolet Blazer EV with different styling, Only introduced for 2024, the Prologue was canceled after 2026 following slow sales. Furthermore, Honda ceased its own EV efforts as market conditions evolved. It will now focus more on hybrids instead of all-electric vehicles. articles.title: Remittances towards overseas equity and debt more than double YoY in August: RBI data
articles.desc: Outward remittances by Indians under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) reached $2738.58 million in August 2026, a 3.6 per cent growth YoY and 6 per cent up from July
articles.content: Remittances towards overseas equity and debt more than double y-o-y in August: RBI data - The HinduBusinessLine 23 days after new RBI forex rules, individual service exporters still await clarity, banks lack SOPs India-US bond yield gap tops 250 bps as G-Sec yield hits 7.48%; FPI inflows uncertain Statistics Min proposes changes in PLFS to include unpaid work, better capture digital platform workers Infosys cuts FY27 growth guidance to 1-2% amid weak demand environment Government asks industry bodies to tighten certification checks, conduct regular cybersecurity audits Remittances towards overseas equity and debt more than double y-o-y in August: RBI data Outward remittances by Indians under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) reached $2738.58 million in August 2026, a 3.6 per cent growth YoY and 6 per cent up from July https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/remittances-towards-overseas-equity-and-debt-more-than-double-yoy-in-august-rbi-data/article71616863.ece Outward remittances by Indians under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) reached $2738.58 million in August, a 3.6 per cent growth YoY and 6 per cent up from July | Photo Credit: SUKREE SUKPLANG Outflows towards investment in equity and debt led the outward remittance in August and are now a much bigger part of the LRS basket compared to last year, RBI data released on Friday show. Outward remittances by Indians under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) reached $2738.58 million in August 2026, a 3.6 per cent growth YoY and 6 per cent up from July, as per the RBI bulletin released on Friday. Remittances for investment in overseas equity and debt more than doubled, rising 111 per cent from $152.18 million in August 2025 to $321.53 million. However, on a month-on-month basis, the total outflow in this category posted a 7 per cent decline. Investment in equity and debt abroad hit an all-time high of $460 million in June. In August 2026, the category accounted for about 11.7 per cent of total LRS outflows in August 2026, up from 5.8 per cent a year earlier. Analysts note that beyond foreign equity markets, there has also been an increased appetite for dollar-linked fixed income investments given the depreciation of the rupee. Excluding the outflow due to investment in equity/debt, the LRS remittances would have declined about 3% year on year. Travel, another major category under the LRS, was flat YoY but strong MoM. Travel accounted for $1630.26 million, or roughly 59.5 per cent of the total in August 2026. This grew by just about 1 per cent from a year ago but climbed 11.4% from July’s $1463.11 million. On a month-on-month basis, business travel zoomed by almost 5x from $10.9 million in July to $51 million in August. Among the other smaller heads, remittance towards deposits rose 18.8 per cent year-on-year to $50.78 million and gifts abroad also grew 13.3 per cent to $215.72 million. Remittances for medical treatment were up 21.3 per cent year on year at $4.84 million, and people spent 1.2 per cent higher towards maintenance of relatives abroad at $275.43 million. articles.title: FirstHoldCo posts ₦744.5bn profit in 9 months as electronic banking fees hit ₦73.2bn
articles.desc: FirstHoldCo Plc, the parent company of FirstBank Nigeria, reported a profit of ₦744.5 billion for the nine months…
articles.content: FirstHoldCo posts ₦744.5bn profit in 9 months as electronic banking fees hit ₦73.2bn FirstHoldCo posts ₦744.5bn profit in 9 months as electronic banking fees hit ₦73.2bn , the parent company of FirstBank Nigeria, reported a profit of ₦744.5 billion for the nine months ending September 30, 2026. This represents a significant increase from the ₦450.9 billion recorded during the same period in 2025. In total, the group made about ₦293.6 billion more in profit than it did a year earlier, a 65.1% increase. Its unaudited financial statements also showed higher earnings from electronic banking and funds transfer services, which are closely linked to customers’ everyday banking activities. However, the jump in profit was much larger than the increase in these fees. This suggests that other areas of the business also played an important role in strengthening the group’s performance. An important factor was the drop in impairment charges. Banks record these charges as a provision for loans and other financial assets that may not be recovered. For FirstHoldCo, impairment charges fell to ₦207.1 billion from ₦288.9 billion a year earlier, representing a decline of about 28.3%. The group also recovered ₦94.3 billion during the period, compared with just ₦5.9 billion in the first nine months of 2025. These recoveries came from loans and other financial exposures that had previously been considered risky or unlikely to be repaid. FirstHoldCo generated ₦76.6 billion from digital channels in H1 2026 Together, the lower impairment charges and sharp rise in recoveries helped support FirstHoldCo’s stronger profit. However, they do not tell the whole story, as the group’s overall performance was also shaped by income from other parts of the business. Electronic banking fees rise to ₦73.2 billion FirstHoldCo earned ₦73.2 billion from electronic banking fees in the nine months to September 2026, compared with ₦68.8 billion in the same period last year. That represents an increase of ₦4.4 billion, or about 6.3%. Electronic banking fees are income generated from services that enable customers to conduct transactions through electronic banking channels. These can include digital banking services and electronic transactions, although the financial statement does not break the category down by individual channel. The increase means this category generated more fee income for the group than it did a year earlier. It does not, however, establish that mobile banking usage or transaction volumes grew by the same percentage. FirstHoldCo’s funds transfer fees also increased The group also earned ₦40.1 billion from funds transfer and intermediation fees in the first nine months of 2026, up from ₦37.0 billion during the same period in 2025. That represents an increase of ₦3.2 billion, or about 8.5%. These fees come from services such as transferring money and helping customers complete transactions. Although such activities may seem routine, the charges provide banks with income in addition to the interest they earn from loans. Combined, electronic banking and funds transfer fees brought in ₦113.3 billion during the period, compared with ₦105.8 billion a year earlier, a 7.1% increase. However, this figure covers only these two fee categories and does not represent FirstHoldCo’s total digital banking revenue. The figures show that while transaction-related income increased, it did not grow nearly as fast as the group’s overall profit, which rose by 65.1%. This means other areas, including lending, loan recoveries, lower impairment charges, operating costs and other income, also contributed to the stronger result. For customers, the results show how everyday activities such as transfers and electronic payments contribute to the wider business of one of Nigeria’s biggest banking groups. articles.title: TG Therapeutics Announces Phase 1 Data Evaluating Azer-cel in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis in a Late-Breaking Oral Presentation at MSToronto2026
articles.content: TG Therapeutics Announces Phase 1 Data Evaluating Azer-cel in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis in a Late-Breaking Oral Presentation at MSToronto2026 | Healthcare | postregister.com You have permission to edit this article. NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 23, 2026-- TG Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: TGTX), today announced initial results from the Company’s Phase 1 study evaluating azercabtagene zapreleucel (azer-cel), an investigational, allogeneic CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, in patients with progressive multiple sclerosis (MS). The data represent the first reported clinical evaluation of an allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy in progressive MS and were presented in a late-breaking oral session at MSToronto2026, the 10th Joint Meeting of the Americas and European Committees for Treatment and Research in Multiple Sclerosis (ACTRIMS-ECTRIMS), being held October 21–23, 2026, in Toronto, Canada. Michael S. Weiss, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TG Therapeutics, stated, “These initial azer-cel results are particularly encouraging given that all patients entered the study with progressive disability despite prior treatment with high-efficacy therapies, including anti-CD20 treatment. The safety findings to date, together with evidence of B-cell depletion in both the blood and cerebrospinal fluid, demonstrate biological activity at doses that appear tolerable, while stable or improved disability scores in most subjects provide a potential signal of clinical activity. Of particular interest, five of the 18 evaluable patients experienced improvements in disability scores, including three patients with improvements of two or more points on the EDSS scale, an encouraging early finding in a disease where even slowing progression can represent an important therapeutic advance.” Mr. Weiss continued, “While these results remain preliminary, we believe an off-the-shelf CAR T-cell therapy has the potential to offer a meaningful new treatment option for patients with progressive MS, where substantial unmet need remains. We look forward to continuing dose escalation and evaluating longer-term outcomes, and we are grateful to the patients, their families, and the clinical teams who are making this research possible.” First Clinical Evaluation of an Allogeneic CD19-Directed CAR T-Cell Therapy in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: Initial Results from the Phase 1 TG-Azercel-101 Study The presentation includes data from 26 participants with progressive MS treated across six azer-cel dose levels, ranging from 30 million to 500 million CAR T-cells, following bendamustine lymphodepletion. All participants had experienced progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) within the prior 12 months despite high-efficacy disease-modifying therapy, and all had previously received anti-CD20 therapy. The median baseline EDSS score was 6.0, reflecting substantial disability, with patients typically requiring assistance to walk even relatively short distances. As of the September 3, 2026 data cutoff, median follow-up was 4.9 months, with a range of 0.1 to 15.0 months. Azer-cel demonstrated an encouraging initial safety profile in 26 participants, with no dose-limiting toxicities or high-grade CAR T associated toxicities observed across dose levels including no Grade ≥3 cytokine release syndrome (CRS), Grade ≥2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS), graft-versus-host disease, immune effector cell-associated hemophagocytic syndrome (IEC-HS) and no Grade ≥3 infections. Despite documented progression prior to enrollment, EDSS scores were stable or improved in 89% of evaluable participants at Day 90 (16/18) and 88% at Day 180 (7/8). Three participants achieved EDSS improvements of at least 2.0 points at Day 90, including one with a 4.0-point improvement. Compared with treatments without the particles, degradation rate constants rose by 1.2 to 1.8 times. Aging left persistent free radi
articles.content: A research team found that aged polyamide microplastics accelerated the breakdown of the pharmaceutical carbamazepine in three ultraviolet-based wastewater treatments. Compared with treatments without the particles, degradation rate constants rose by 1.2 to 1.8 times. Aging left persistent free radicals on the plastic surfaces, helping generate reactive species that attacked the drug. Faster removal, however, did not guarantee a safer outcome: some transformation products were predicted to be more toxic than carbamazepine itself. The findings could help wastewater engineers assess treatment performance by tracking both the disappearance of a drug and the compounds produced as it breaks down.

articles.title: Daily Spectral Fingerprints Reveal Hidden Genetics of Poplar Growth
articles.desc: A research team has shown that daily hyperspectral measurements can expose how genetic differences shape photosynthesis, seasonal change, and growth in black cottonwood, Populus trichocarpa, under field drought conditions. By pairing repeated canopy spectra with genome-wide association studies, the
articles.content: A research team has shown that daily hyperspectral measurements can expose how genetic differences shape photosynthesis, seasonal change, and growth in black cottonwood, Populus trichocarpa, under field drought conditions. By pairing repeated canopy spectra with genome-wide association studies, the researchers traced genetic signals across the growing season rather than relying on a single snapshot. The work links specific blue and red wavelengths to pigment biology, identifies chloroplast-related candidate genes, and shows that spectral data can help predict tree growth. The approach could make field phenotyping faster, less destructive, and more informative for breeding productive, resilient bioenergy trees under changing environmental conditions.
